name: Premier League
formatSummary: Single round-robin league, no groups, no playoffs for title.
knockoutStructure: None for title; relegation is by final league position.
finalFormat: No final; champion is team with most points after 38 matches.

name: EFL Championship
formatSummary: Single round-robin league with promotion playoffs.
knockoutStructure: Promotion playoffs for 3rd-6th placed teams (semi-finals two legs, final single match at Wembley).
finalFormat: Playoff final is single match; winner promoted to Premier League.

name: EFL League One
formatSummary: Single round-robin league with promotion playoffs.
knockoutStructure: Playoffs for 3rd-6th (semi-finals two legs, final single).

name: EFL League Two
formatSummary: Single round-robin league with promotion playoffs.
knockoutStructure: Playoffs for 4th-7th (semi-finals two legs, final single).

name: FA Cup
formatSummary: Straight knockout from early rounds, some replays in early stages (historically), later rounds single match.
typicalParticipants: 700+ clubs across all levels (qualifying + main draw).
knockoutStructure: Entire tournament is knockout; early rounds include qualifying, then Proper Rounds 1-6, semis, final.

name: EFL Cup (Carabao Cup)
formatSummary: Knockout tournament for Premier League and EFL clubs.
knockoutStructure: All rounds knockout; early rounds single match, semis traditionally two legs (format may vary by season).

name: FA Community Shield
formatSummary: Single match between Premier League champions and FA Cup winners (or league runners-up if same team wins double).
finalFormat: Single match; if draw, usually decided by penalties.

name: Women’s Super League (WSL)
formatSummary: Round-robin league.

name: Women’s FA Cup
formatSummary: Knockout cup for women’s clubs.
typicalParticipants: Multiple tiers, hundreds of clubs in qualifying + main draw.

name: La Liga
formatSummary: Round-robin league.

name: Copa del Rey
formatSummary: Knockout tournament, some early rounds single leg, later rounds often two legs until final.
knockoutStructure: Entirely knockout; early rounds may have two-leg ties, final single.

name: Supercopa de España
formatSummary: Mini-tournament (semi-finals + final) featuring league and cup winners/runners-up.

name: Bundesliga
formatSummary: Round-robin league.

name: DFB-Pokal
formatSummary: Straight knockout.

name: DFL-Supercup
formatSummary: Single match between Bundesliga champion and DFB-Pokal winner.

name: Serie A
formatSummary: Round-robin league.

name: Coppa Italia
formatSummary: Knockout tournament, some early rounds single leg, later rounds two legs until final.
knockoutStructure: Knockout; early rounds single, semis two legs, final single.
finalFormat: Single match at neutral venue (often Rome).

name: Supercoppa Italiana
formatSummary: Single match or mini-tournament (recently 4-team).

name: Ligue 1
formatSummary: Round-robin league.

name: Coupe de France
formatSummary: Nationwide knockout, includes amateur clubs.
typicalParticipants: 7,000+ clubs in early rounds; main draw ~64.
finalFormat: Single match at Stade de France.

name: Trophée des Champions
formatSummary: Single match between Ligue 1 champion and Coupe de France winner.

name: UEFA Champions League
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.
typicalParticipants: 32-36 clubs (format evolving; top clubs from UEFA associations).
knockoutStructure: Round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals (two legs each), final single.
finalFormat: Single match at pre-selected neutral venue; extra time + penalties if needed.

name: UEFA Europa League
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.
typicalParticipants: ~32 clubs (domestic cup winners, league runners-up, drop-down from UCL).
knockoutStructure: Knockout round playoffs, R16, QF, SF (two legs), final single.

name: UEFA Europa Conference League
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout, lower tier than UEL.
knockoutStructure: Knockout round playoffs, R16, QF, SF (two legs), final single.

name: UEFA Super Cup
formatSummary: Single match between Champions League and Europa League winners.

name: Copa Libertadores
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.
typicalParticipants: 32-47 clubs (varies by format), top clubs from CONMEBOL associations.
knockoutStructure: R16, QF, SF (two legs), final single (neutral venue).

name: Copa Sudamericana
formatSummary: Knockout from early rounds; some editions include group phase.

name: CONMEBOL Recopa
formatSummary: Two-legged tie between Libertadores and Sudamericana winners.
finalFormat: Aggregate over two legs; away goals/penalties if needed.

name: CAF Champions League
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.
typicalParticipants: 16 clubs in group stage from CAF members.
knockoutStructure: QF, SF (two legs), final two legs (home & away).
finalFormat: Two-leg final; aggregate score decides winner.

name: CAF Confederation Cup
formatSummary: Similar to Champions League, second-tier.

name: CAF Super Cup
formatSummary: Single match between Champions League and Confederation Cup winners.

name: CONCACAF Champions Cup (formerly Champions League)
formatSummary: Knockout tournament (some editions include group stage).
knockoutStructure: Multi-round knockout; final two legs in recent formats.

name: Leagues Cup
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout featuring MLS and Liga MX clubs.
knockoutStructure: Group stage, then R32, R16, QF, SF, final (single matches).
finalFormat: Single final at neutral or pre-selected venue.

name: CONCACAF Central American Cup / Caribbean Cup (qualifiers for Champions Cup)
formatSummary: Group + knockout qualifiers for Champions Cup.
knockoutStructure: Group stage then knockout to allocate Champions Cup slots.

name: AFC Champions League
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.
knockoutStructure: R16, QF, SF, final (format varies; often two legs).

name: AFC Cup (second-tier)
formatSummary: Group + knockout for lower-ranked associations.
knockoutStructure: Group stage, then knockout to final.
finalFormat: Single or two-leg final depending on edition.

name: FIFA World Cup
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.
knockoutStructure: R16, QF, SF, final; single-elimination after groups.
finalFormat: Single final at neutral host nation; extra time + penalties if needed.

name: FIFA Women’s World Cup
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: UEFA European Championship (Euros)
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: UEFA Nations League
formatSummary: League groups + finals.
typicalParticipants: All UEFA members split into leagues (A, B, C, D).
frequency: Biennial cycle with finals every 2 years.
knockoutStructure: League A group winners advance to 4-team finals (semis + final).

name: Copa América
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON)
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: CONCACAF Gold Cup
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: AFC Asian Cup
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: OFC Nations Cup
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout (or round-robin final stage in some editions).

name: FIFA Confederations Cup (discontinued after 2017)
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: Olympic Football Tournament (Men & Women)
formatSummary: Group stage + knockout.

name: Rugby World Cup (Men)
formatSummary: Pool stage + knockout.
finalFormat: Single final at host nation; extra time + kicks if needed.

name: Rugby World Cup (Women)
formatSummary: Pool stage + knockout.

name: Six Nations Championship
formatSummary: Round-robin league between 6 nations (England, France, Ireland, Italy, Scotland, Wales).
knockoutStructure: None; champion by points. Tie-breakers apply.
finalFormat: No final; Grand Slam if one team beats all others.

name: The Rugby Championship
formatSummary: Round-robin (home & away) between Argentina, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa.
finalFormat: No final; champion by competition points and tie-breakers.

name: Nations Championship
formatSummary: Cross-hemisphere league fixtures followed by a finals weekend.
typicalParticipants: 12 leading nations: Six Nations sides plus Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan, New Zealand and South Africa.
knockoutStructure: Teams are ranked after scheduled cross-hemisphere matches; ranking matches are played at finals weekend.
finalFormat: Single ranking/final matches at the designated finals venue.

name: British & Irish Lions Tour
formatSummary: Tour matches culminating in a Test series against Australia, New Zealand or South Africa.
typicalParticipants: British & Irish Lions and one host national team, plus provincial/club opponents.
finalFormat: Usually a three-Test series; series decided by match wins.

name: European Rugby Champions Cup
formatSummary: Pool phase followed by knockout rugby.
typicalParticipants: Leading clubs from Premiership Rugby, Top 14 and United Rugby Championship.
knockoutStructure: Round of 16, quarter-finals and semi-finals, all single matches.
finalFormat: Single final at a pre-selected venue.

name: United Rugby Championship
region: Ireland, Italy, Scotland, South Africa and Wales
formatSummary: League phase followed by playoffs.
knockoutStructure: Top eight enter single-match quarter-finals and semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single Grand Final hosted according to competition rules.

name: Premiership Rugby
formatSummary: League season followed by playoffs.
typicalParticipants: Top-flight English professional clubs; number can vary by season.
knockoutStructure: Leading teams qualify for single-match semi-finals.

name: Top 14
formatSummary: Home-and-away league followed by playoffs.
finalFormat: Single final, normally at Stade de France.

name: Super Rugby Pacific
formatSummary: League phase followed by playoffs.
typicalParticipants: Professional franchises from Australia, New Zealand and Pacific nations; count varies by season.
knockoutStructure: Qualifying teams contest quarter-finals and semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single Grand Final hosted by the higher-ranked finalist under current rules.

name: Rugby League World Cup (Men)
formatSummary: Pool stage followed by knockout matches.
finalFormat: Single final at a host-nation venue.

name: Rugby League World Cup (Women)
formatSummary: Two groups followed by knockout matches.
knockoutStructure: Top two in each group progress to semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single final at a host-nation venue.

name: Super League
formatSummary: Regular season followed by playoffs.
typicalParticipants: Top-level professional clubs; participant count may vary by season.
knockoutStructure: Highest-ranked clubs qualify for elimination playoffs and semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single Grand Final at Old Trafford.

name: Challenge Cup
formatSummary: Open knockout cup.
typicalParticipants: Professional, semi-professional and community clubs enter at staged rounds.
finalFormat: Single final at a designated national stadium.

name: National Rugby League (NRL)
formatSummary: Regular season followed by an eight-team finals series.
knockoutStructure: Qualifying and elimination finals, semi-finals and preliminary finals.

name: State of Origin
formatSummary: Three-match series between Queensland and New South Wales.
finalFormat: Best-of-three series; aggregate score is not used.

name: World Club Challenge
formatSummary: Showpiece match between the Super League and NRL champions.
finalFormat: Single match, with extra time if required.

name: Australian Open
formatSummary: Seeded singles and doubles draws played as straight knockout.
typicalParticipants: Singles main draws usually contain 128 players; doubles and qualifying draws are separate.
knockoutStructure: Successive elimination rounds from the opening round to semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single championship match; match length and deciding-set rules follow event and draw rules.

name: French Open (Roland-Garros)
formatSummary: Seeded singles and doubles draws played as straight knockout.
typicalParticipants: Singles main draws usually contain 128 players; doubles and qualifying draws are separate.
knockoutStructure: Successive elimination rounds from the opening round to semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single championship match; match length and deciding-set rules follow event and draw rules.

name: Wimbledon
formatSummary: Seeded singles and doubles draws played as straight knockout.
typicalParticipants: Singles main draws usually contain 128 players; doubles and qualifying draws are separate.
knockoutStructure: Successive elimination rounds from the opening round to semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single championship match; match length and deciding-set rules follow event and draw rules.

name: US Open
formatSummary: Seeded singles and doubles draws played as straight knockout.
typicalParticipants: Singles main draws usually contain 128 players; doubles and qualifying draws are separate.
knockoutStructure: Successive elimination rounds from the opening round to semi-finals.
finalFormat: Single championship match; match length and deciding-set rules follow event and draw rules.

name: ATP Finals
formatSummary: Two round-robin groups followed by knockout matches.
typicalParticipants: Top 8 eligible men in singles and top 8 doubles teams.
knockoutStructure: Top two from each group reach semi-finals.

name: WTA Finals
formatSummary: Two round-robin groups followed by knockout matches.
typicalParticipants: Top 8 eligible women in singles and top 8 doubles teams.
knockoutStructure: Top two from each group reach semi-finals.

name: Davis Cup
formatSummary: Home-or-away team ties lead to a Final 8 knockout event.
typicalParticipants: National men's teams qualify through tiered competition.
finalFormat: A team tie decided by scheduled singles and doubles rubbers.

name: Billie Jean King Cup
formatSummary: Qualifying ties lead to an eight-team Finals event.
knockoutStructure: Finals use a straight knockout bracket from quarter-finals.
finalFormat: A team tie decided by singles and doubles rubbers.

name: Olympic Tennis Tournament
formatSummary: Men's and women's singles and doubles, plus mixed doubles, in knockout draws.
typicalParticipants: Qualified players representing National Olympic Committees.
finalFormat: Single gold-medal match in each event.

name: ICC Men's Cricket World Cup
formatSummary: 50-over group/league phase followed by knockouts.
typicalParticipants: National teams qualifying through the ICC pathway; participant count varies by edition.
finalFormat: Single final at a host venue.

name: ICC Women's Cricket World Cup
formatSummary: 50-over league/group phase followed by knockouts.

name: ICC Men's T20 World Cup
formatSummary: Twenty20 group stages followed by knockouts.
typicalParticipants: Qualified national teams; participant count varies by edition.

name: ICC Women's T20 World Cup
formatSummary: Twenty20 group stage followed by knockouts.

name: ICC Champions Trophy
formatSummary: Short 50-over tournament with groups followed by knockouts.
frequency: Periodic within the ICC event cycle.

name: ICC World Test Championship
formatSummary: Multi-year Test league cycle.
typicalParticipants: Leading Test-playing nations; each plays a scheduled subset of series.
knockoutStructure: No semi-finals under the current format.
finalFormat: Single Test final at a designated neutral venue.

name: The Ashes
formatSummary: Test series between England and Australia.
typicalParticipants: 2 men's national teams; a separate Women's Ashes is also contested.
finalFormat: Series decided by Test wins; the holder retains the urn if the series is drawn.

name: Indian Premier League (IPL)
formatSummary: Twenty20 league phase followed by playoffs.

name: The Hundred
formatSummary: 100-ball league with separate men's and women's competitions.
typicalParticipants: 8 city-based teams in each competition under the established format.
knockoutStructure: Top team advances to final; second and third contest an Eliminator.
